claude-s · type-film

Count the gap: a type film cut to the speed of sound

Make an original 10 s kinetic-type film about counting from lightning to thunder. Real numbers only (sound at 343 m/s, about 3 s per kilometre), no music, no corner HUD. The type should behave like the storm.

What the skill did

  • The edit's clock is the speed of sound. Each thunder lands distance / 343 s after its flash: 2.92 s for 1 km, 1.0 s for 343 m, and no gap overhead. The picture and the sound script read the same cue list.
  • Type set by the skill's new measured rules. The counted numerals grow from 20 to 28 to 44 % of frame height as the storm closes in. The answers stand 38–48 % tall, and the last 0 fills 95 %. An italic serif lead sits over a 900-weight condensed grotesk, placed by its ink (fitStack, inkBox), and each word lands oversized and settles (hitWord).
  • Each flash inverts the frame: a stepped white-out with a re-stroke, and the bolt drawn as one tapered fill. Its afterimage is the film's only colour, a hi-vis lime that straightens into the rule GO INSIDE stands on.
  • The rain is drawCloud: 440 to 760 streaks whose size, brightness and streak length all come from one depth. It gets denser after each thunder, and drops on the lens glint only in the flash.
  • Three rounds with a fresh critic. Grey flashes became hard white ones, beaded strokes became one filled taper, the lead lines doubled in size, a fading afterimage became a held one, and the answers moved onto the thunder's rolls.
  • Second video: the skill's earlier claude-s film (screen HUD, iso skyline, a single-take morph), kept for comparison.

Sound

  • No music: rain, thunder synthesised per distance (darker and later far away, with a 2–5 kHz crack and a sub only up close), and a knuckle tap on each counted second.
  • The flashes are silent on purpose, because light arrives first. After the overhead strike come 0.7 s of digital silence, then the rain returns and the storm's last roll lands under INSIDE.
